summary: Request: Near-real-time Splunk HEC export with per-tenant pseudonymization, signed manifest, and KMS rotation proof
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (FinlyBank Inc.) requests a near-real-time SIEM export to their Splunk HEC endpoint with the following requirements: per-tenant pseudonymization of user identifiers (deterministic, salted hash with per-tenant salt), field-level redaction for PII (SSN/email), a signed delivery manifest (PKCS7 preferred) for each hourly bundle, and an auditable key-rotation proof that shows evidence of KMS key changes over the retention period. They also report a discrepancy in daily event counts between Redwood's audit export and their Splunk index for 2026-02-20 to 2026-03-04, which they want reconciled as part of the evidence package.

Impact:
- Security/compliance team at FinlyBank cannot close their internal SOC2 evidence package without a signed manifest and rotation proof.
- They treat this as time-sensitive due to an upcoming audit window.

Customer ask (explicit):
1) Design and deliver a temporary signed-hourly S3 dump + manifest that includes: SHA256 checksums for each file, PKCS7 signed manifest, sample redacted payloads (3 examples), and a CSV reconciliation showing per-hour counts.
2) Provide KMS rotation history and attestable proofs (key version IDs, rotation timestamps, and signed audit entries) for the last 90 days.
3) Advice and timeline for a permanent Splunk HEC connector supporting per-tenant envelope encryption and HEC ingestion with backpressure/ack semantics.
4) Reconcile the event-count discrepancy for 2026-02-20 -> 2026-03-04 and supply a remediation plan.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted (prod) exports to customer Splunk HEC endpoint via outbound TLS (customer-managed endpoint). Region: us-east.
- Customer uses enterprise tier with VPC peering and static egress IP allowlist.

Steps to validate (proposed):
1) Support prepares sample hourly S3 export for 2026-03-09 00:00-03:00 UTC with PKCS7 manifest and provides presigned URLs to customer.
2) Customer verifies manifest signature and per-file checksums; validates redaction on sample payloads.
3) Support provides KMS rotation log entries and signed attestations; customer verifies continuity of key lineage.

Observed vs Expected:
- Observed: Customer reports ~8-12% fewer events indexed in Splunk for certain hours; missing records appear correlated with peak ingest windows.
- Expected: The export should be lossless for audit events and any dropped events should be captured in a delivery failure log with retry metadata.

Attachments:
- Splunk HEC debug headers (provided by customer) and sample indexed events (redacted). Links included in comments.

Notes: This ticket will become part of the formal evidence bundle; please include clear steps and a signed manifest for archival.
comments: Lina Chen (FinlyBank - Security) 2026-03-10: We're preparing our SOC2 folder and need a signed manifest + rotation proof before 2026-03-15. We can accept temporary S3 links for now; long-term HEC is preferred. Also attaching Splunk index screenshots and HEC ingestion logs. (link: https://files.finlybank.com/attachments/finly-splunk-evidence-2026-03-10.zip)

Marco Gutierrez (Support) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged — assigning to SRE for delivery pipeline check and to Security Eng for manifest/key proof. SLA noted for 2026-03-13. Will follow up with ETA for temporary S3 bundle by end of day 2026-03-11.

Devon Morales (SRE) 2026-03-11: Initial triage — audit-service delivery metrics show increased retry count between 2026-02-25 18:00 UTC and 2026-02-27 06:00 UTC for that customer's tenant due to transient 502 responses from the HEC endpoint. We are pulling retry logs and will generate reconciliation CSV for hourly sent vs acked. Suspect backpressure and connection resets at peak.

Marco Gutierrez (Support) 2026-03-12: Temporary S3 bundle uploaded: presigned urls emailed to Lina. Manifest signed with PKCS7 (signature key id: redwood-export-signing-v1). KMS rotation log excerpt attached in Confluence page. Long-term design/estimate posted to the HEC connector design doc for review.

Sven Johansson (Security Eng) 2026-03-12: Verified PKCS7 signature on manifest and validated SHA256 checksums for the sample files. KMS rotation proof included key version map and rotation timestamps. We recommend retention of signed manifests for 180 days for audit purposes.
investigation_notes: Checked delivery logs for tenant finlybank-tenant-42: increased 5xx responses from customer HEC between 2026-02-25T18:10Z and 2026-02-26T02:45Z.

Retry subsystem queued ~18k events that were successfully retried after the endpoint recovered; however, some retries exceeded our max-backoff window and were written to 'failed-deliveries' S3 bucket — those correspond to missing events seen by customer.
Hypothesis: combination of aggressive client-side backoff + intermittent network resets on customer side led to transient drops; root cause needs coordinated network trace with customer infra team.
Verified that current export manifest generation includes SHA256 and UTC timestamps but not PKCS7 by default; implemented one-off PKCS7 signing using redwood-export-signing-v1 for temporary bundle.
KMS rotation proof: exported CloudKMS audit entries (signatures of rotation), matched key-version IDs to artifact signatures; will provide canonicalized CSV with rotation history.
resolution:
Workaround delivered: Temporary signed S3 bundles provided (PKCS7 manifest, per-file SHA256 checksums, and three redacted sample payloads). Reconciliation CSV detailing hourly sent, acked, retried, and permanently failed counts for 2026-02-20 -> 2026-03-04 attached to Confluence. KMS rotation proof exported as signed CSV and uploaded to Confluence.

Permanent plan / next steps:
1) Build first-class Splunk HEC connector that supports per-tenant envelope encryption and deterministic salted hashing for identifiers; include explicit ack/backpressure handling and a persistent delivery ledger to avoid silent drops. Planned PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/siem-connectors/pull/198 (design is drafted).
2) Add PKCS7 manifest generation to the audit-service as an opt-in export mode; implement retention policy for manifests and signed archives (proposal: 180 days).
3) Implement improved retry semantics and alerting for tenant-level delivery failures, and add a dashboard in Console for per-tenant delivery success rate.
4) Coordinate a joint network trace session with FinlyBank infra for 2026-03-15 to validate connection stability under load.

Follow-ups: Marco to schedule an engineering design review (ETA 2026-03-18) and a security handoff meeting to sign off on per-tenant salt handling. Ticket will be updated with PR numbers and rollout dates.
resolution_notes: Temporary deliverables accepted by customer on 2026-03-12. Customer confirmed PKCS7 manifest validated and reconciled counts matched provided reconciliation CSV for flagged hours. Next milestone: HEC connector design review 2026-03-18.
